classification.difficultyReason: Apply exact ratios to individual triangles and subtract lengths in compound diagrams.

content.prompt: Find the exact value of $x$ in these diagrams.

spec.description: Unshaded right triangle with horizontal base 6, vertical right side x, bottom-right right-angle marker and top-right 60-degree angle.
spec.mathematics: The base is opposite 60 degrees and x is adjacent. Coordinate proportions satisfy tan 60 degrees = 6/x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown x are visible.

spec.description: Upright equilateral triangle. Each side carries a single equality tick and the label 4. An external vertical double-headed arrow marks height x.
spec.mathematics: The triangle has three equal sides and 60-degree angles. The external height arrow spans exactly from base level to apex level.
spec.answerVisibility: No altitude, derived angle or answer is supplied in the question figure.

answer.worked:
The triangle is equilateral, so each angle is $60^\circ$. Draw the perpendicular altitude to form two right-angled triangles.
$$\begin{align*}\sin60^\circ&=\frac{x}{4}\\x&=4\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\\x&=2\sqrt{3}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right triangle with base 9, vertical left side and an internal segment from the lower-right vertex to the left side. The upper vertical segment is x. The lower-right angle is divided into 30 degrees below the internal segment and 15 degrees above it, with a leader for the 15-degree label.
spec.mathematics: The outer lower-right angle is 45 degrees. The full vertical height is 9 and the lower vertical height is 9 tan 30 degrees = 3 sqrt(3).
spec.answerVisibility: The 45-degree total and derived heights are absent from the student figure.

answer.short: $x=9-3\sqrt{3}$. Subtract the lower height $9\tan30^\circ$ from the full height $9\tan45^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The outer angle at the bottom-right vertex is $30^\circ+15^\circ=45^\circ$. Let $H$ be the full vertical height and $h$ the lower vertical height.
$$\begin{align*}H&=9\tan45^\circ\\H&=9\\h&=9\tan30^\circ\\h&=\frac{9}{\sqrt{3}}=3\sqrt{3}\\x&=H-h\\x&=9-3\sqrt{3}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right triangle with left vertical side 20. An internal segment joins the top-left vertex to an intermediate base point. The inner base angle is 45 degrees and the outer base angle is 30 degrees. A double-headed horizontal arrow beneath the base identifies x as the segment between the two base endpoints.
spec.mathematics: The full base is 20/tan 30 degrees and the shorter base is 20/tan 45 degrees; x is their difference.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 20, 45 degrees, 30 degrees and unknown x are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ be the full base and $l$ the shorter base ending at the internal segment.
$$\begin{align*}\tan30^\circ&=\frac{20}{L}\\L&=\frac{20}{1/\sqrt{3}}=20\sqrt{3}\\\tan45^\circ&=\frac{20}{l}\\l&=20\\x&=L-l\\x&=20\sqrt{3}-20\end{align*}$$
